# Hydrostatic and well-balanced treatment {#sec-ch05}

A stratified atmosphere at rest is the state snapy's $x_1$ sweep has to leave alone, and it is the hardest one:
its pressure and density change by orders of magnitude along $x_1$, while the motions of interest are small
perturbations of it. This chapter describes how the $x_1$ reconstruction keeps such a column at rest to round-off
and how close the reference it uses comes to the column's own profile. It covers, in the order the code builds
them: the well-balanced $x_1$ reconstruction, which reconstructs perturbations about a discretely hydrostatic
reference; the reference kernel, which builds that reference from a top-down pressure scan; its closure at a
physical wall; its continuity across $x_1$ block seams; the hydrostatic mode, which replaces gravity by the cell's
own pressure difference; `balance_column`, which projects an initial column onto the scheme's discrete balance;
the fourth-order reference `SNAP_WB_REF4`; the $r^2$-exact $x_1$ maps `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` of spherical-polar
grids; what is left of the $1/R$ term after them; and two legacy wall routines. The gravity work these schemes are
used with is Chapter 6 (@sec-ch06); the switches and their tested combinations are Chapter 12.

All derivations of this chapter are checked by one executable check, `src/snapy_report/ch05/wbref_check.py`,
whose output `wbref_check.out` carries the claim tags `[C1]`–`[C21]`; claim `[C11]` is an independent rebuild of
the default reference from the equations of this chapter that reproduces the numbers snapy's own wall test prints.

## Well-balanced $x_1$ reconstruction: perturbations about a hydrostatic reference (gravity on) {#sec-ch05-wbx1}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Reconstructs $p-p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ along $x_1$ instead of $p$ and
$\rho$, then adds the reference face values back, so a discretely hydrostatic column produces no $x_1$ force.
**Switch.** None. On whenever $g_1\neq0$, the state has a pressure row and the EOS is not `shallow-water`; also
under an $x_1$ block split.
**Requires.** The reference kernel (@sec-ch05-refkernel).
**Order.** Exact rest balance; the face states keep the order of the reconstruction.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-wbx1-split.
:::

A column in hydrostatic balance has pressure and density that fall by orders of magnitude along $x_1$. A high-order
reconstruction of $p$ itself returns face values whose difference across a cell is not exactly $\rho g_1\Delta x_1$,
so a resting column feels a spurious vertical force of the size of the reconstruction error and starts to move.
snapy removes that force by construction: it builds, on every call, a reference $(p_{\mathrm{ref}},
\rho_{\mathrm{ref}})$ whose face pressures satisfy the discrete hydrostatic balance exactly, reconstructs only the
perturbations about it, and restores the reference at the faces. The perturbation of a resting column is a constant,
which every reconstruction reproduces, so the restored faces carry exactly the balanced pressure difference.

The scheme has no switch and no default to change: it is the $x_1$ path whenever gravity acts in $x_1$. The
perturbation ghosts at a physical, non-outflow $x_1$ wall are filled with even parity; the reconstruction runs with
its density and pressure floors off; and a face value that comes out non-positive falls back to the reference
pressure or to the density of the adjacent cell. The $x_2$ and $x_3$ sweeps have no such treatment.

*Aliases.* "WB" or "well-balanced reconstruction" in comments and commit messages; the "base" reference of
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §1.

### Derivation

Units: $p$ [Pa], $\rho$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $g_1$ [m s$^{-2}$], $x_1$ and $\Delta x_1$ [m]. This layer uses cell averages
and face point values; a cell average carries an overbar only where a point value of the same quantity appears.

The $x_1$ momentum equation with constant gravity is $\partial_t(\rho v_1)+\partial_1(\rho v_1^2+p)=\rho g_1$.
Integrated over cell $i$ of a Cartesian column, with $p^{*}_{i\pm1/2}$ the face pressures of the Riemann solver,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\overline{\rho v_1})_i = -\frac{\Delta_i[\rho v_1^2+p^{*}]}{\Delta x_1} + \overline{\rho}_i g_1 .
$$

At rest the advective part vanishes and the cell stays at rest exactly when
$p^{*}_{i+1/2}-p^{*}_{i-1/2}=g_1\overline{\rho}_i\Delta x_1$. The reference kernel (@sec-ch05-refkernel) builds face
pressures $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ that satisfy this difference identically, @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan, together with a cell
pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref},i}$, a cell density $\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i}$ and a face density $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$. The
reconstruction then works on the perturbations and restores the reference at the faces:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p'_i &= \overline{p}_i - p_{\mathrm{ref},i}, \\
\rho'_i &= \overline{\rho}_i - \rho_{\mathrm{ref},i}, \\
p^{L,R}_{i-1/2} &= \mathcal R^{L,R}[p']_{i-1/2} + p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}, \\
\rho^{L,R}_{i-1/2} &= \mathcal R^{L,R}[\rho']_{i-1/2} + \rho_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbx1-split}

with $\mathcal R^{L,R}$ the left and right face values of the configured $x_1$ reconstruction. The subtraction in
@eq-ch05-wbx1-split is done by `_hydro_ref_x1` and the two in-place updates that follow it
([`hydro_forward.cpp:288-293`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L288-L293)),
and the restore by `psf_lo` added back to both states
([`hydro_forward.cpp:357-363`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L357-L363)).

Suppose now that $p'_i=c$ in every cell, for one constant $c$, and $v_1=0$. Every reconstruction of snapy returns a
constant exactly, so $p^{L}=p^{R}=p_{\mathrm{sf}}+c$ at every face, the two states agree, and the Riemann solver
returns $p^{*}=p_{\mathrm{sf}}+c$ with zero mass and energy flux. The momentum balance above then reads
$-(p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2}-p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2})/\Delta x_1+\overline{\rho}_ig_1=0$ by @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan. The
discrete rest state of the scheme is therefore

$$
\overline{p}_i = p_{\mathrm{ref},i}(\overline{p},\overline{\rho}) + c \quad\text{in every cell},
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbx1-rest}

whatever the density reference is: with $v_1=0$ the face density enters no flux. Because $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is rebuilt
from the state, @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is a fixed-point condition on the column, which `balance_column` solves
(@sec-ch05-balcol). On spherical-polar grids the face areas and the geometric pressure source enter the same
cancellation; the plain-mean form is @sec-ch05-x1cent. The derivation follows
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §§1, 6.

*Exact and truncated.* The rest balance is exact for any column satisfying @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest. Away from rest the
face states carry the reconstruction's truncation error on the perturbation plus the offset
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal R[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]$ of the density reference, which is $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ for the
default reference (`[C14]`) and $O(\Delta x_1^4)$ with @sec-ch05-wbref4. The identity used in the cancellation,
that the hydrostatic correction and the pressure force cancel at rest, is `[C19]`.

### Numerical method

Where things live: $\overline p$, $\overline\rho$ and the perturbations are cell averages; $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ and
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ are face point values at the lower face of each cell; the reconstructed states are face
values. The scheme runs in every RK stage, in the $x_1$ block of `HydroImpl::forward`, explicitly.

**Ghosts.** At a physical $x_1$ wall whose boundary function is not an outflow, the $n_g$ ghost cells of $p'$ and
$\rho'$ are overwritten with the mirror image of the first $n_g$ interior cells, even parity, while the velocity keeps
the odd ghosts of the reflecting boundary (@fig-ch05-wbx1-ghosts). A resting perturbation ($p'=c$) is then constant
across the wall too. At an $x_1$ seam the ghosts are the neighbour's cells and the reference is made continuous by
@sec-ch05-seam; at an outflow boundary the ghosts are left as the boundary function wrote them.

Bottom row: the normal velocity (black arrows) is mirrored with odd parity. A constant perturbation stays constant across the wall, so a resting column sees no wall force.](05-well-balanced_files/figure-html/fig-ch05-wbx1-ghosts-output-1.svg){#fig-ch05-wbx1-ghosts fig-alt='Two rows of cells with a thick wall line between three hatched ghost cells on the left and three interior cells on the right; circles mirrored at equal heights in the top row, arrows mirrored with reversed direction in the bottom row.'}

**Floors.** The reconstruction of the perturbations is called with `floor=false`, because a perturbation is
legitimately negative and the density and pressure floors would clamp it; the passive-species rows are still
clamped at zero when the EOS limiter is on. After the restore, a non-positive face pressure is replaced by
$p_{\mathrm{sf}}$; a non-positive left density at face $i-\tfrac12$ by $\overline\rho_{i-1}$ and a non-positive
right density by $\overline\rho_i$, the cell on the same side. The adjacent cell, and not $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$, is
used because a reference that overestimates the density aloft turns every floor event at a reflecting top wall into
a large spurious impedance. The shift that builds $\overline\rho_{i-1}$ replicates the first cell instead of
wrapping around the column. @sec-ch08 owns the positivity floors in general.

**Order.** In the interior the face states have the order of the reconstruction applied to a smooth perturbation,
plus the density-reference offset above; at rest the result is exact in interior, wall and seam cells alike. A
column that is not at the fixed point @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest has a residual force of the size of
$p'_i-c$, which is what `balance_column` removes.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The $x_2$ and $x_3$ reconstructions have no well-balanced treatment. A column that is hydrostatic in the continuum
but not at the discrete fixed point @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is not at rest.
:::

1. **No horizontal treatment.** The $x_2$ and $x_3$ sweeps reconstruct the full state

## Hydrostatic reference kernel: face-pressure scan, cell pressure and density reference (with the WB path) {#sec-ch05-refkernel}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Builds, per column and per call, the face pressures $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ by a top-down hydrostatic
scan, the cell pressure $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ from them, and the density references $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ from a smoothed $\rho/p$.
**Switch.** None: always with the well-balanced path (@sec-ch05-wbx1).
**Order.** $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ exact up to one column constant; $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ $O(\Delta x_1^6)$ on uniform grids;
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ $O(\Delta x_1^2)$.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan.
:::

The kernel is the reference of @eq-ch05-wbx1-split. Its face pressures are the discrete hydrostatic balance itself,
summed from an anchor at the top of the column, so the rest balance of the well-balanced reconstruction holds
identically. Its cell pressure is the cell average of a quintic through six face pressures, which matches the
cell average of a smooth hydrostatic pressure to sixth order up to the same column constant; on a non-uniform grid it
is a log-mean instead, exact only for an isothermal cell. Its density reference is the cell pressure times a
smoothed $\rho/p$: smoothed, because an unsmoothed ratio makes the density perturbation a copy of the pressure
perturbation and the entropy mode would bypass the reconstruction.

The kernel has a C++ implementation shared by the CPU and CUDA paths and a tensor implementation for MPS. The wall
closure of the smoothed ratio and of the six-face rows is @sec-ch05-wallclamp; the anchor relay across $x_1$ seams is
@sec-ch05-seam; the fourth-order replacement of the density reference is @sec-ch05-wbref4.

*Aliases.* "smooth5" (the five-point binomial) and "the base reference" in
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §1.

### Derivation

Units as in @sec-ch05-wbx1; $g=-g_1>0$ [m s$^{-2}$] is the downward magnitude the kernel takes; $r=\rho/p$
[s$^2$ m$^{-2}$]. Cell $i$ spans $[x_{1,i-1/2},x_{1,i+1/2}]$, and $\Delta x_{1,i}$ is its width.

#### Face pressures

Hydrostatic balance integrated over cell $i$ gives
$p(x_{1,i-1/2})-p(x_{1,i+1/2})=g\int_{\mathrm{cell}}\rho\,\mathrm{d}x_1=g\,\overline\rho_i\Delta x_{1,i}$ exactly, for
the cell average $\overline\rho_i$. The kernel defines the face pressures by this relation,

$$
p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2} = p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2} + g\,\overline{\rho}_i\,\Delta x_{1,i},
$$ {#eq-ch05-refkernel-scan}

downward from the top face of the top interior cell $i_u$ and upward into the upper ghosts, clipped below at the
smallest positive normal number. @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan is `hydro_ref_x1_scan_impl`
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:22-60`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L22-L60)).
Since each step is exact, $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ equals the exact face pressure of a hydrostatic column plus one constant
per column, set by the anchor (`[C13]`: spread of $p_{\mathrm{sf}}-p(x_{1,f})$ $2.2\times10^{-16}$ of $p$). On a
single block the anchor extrapolates the top cell isothermally by half a cell,

$$
p_{\mathrm{sf},i_u+1/2} = \overline{p}_{i_u}\exp\!\left(-\frac{g\,\Delta x_{1,i_u}}{2\,\overline{p}_{i_u}/\overline{\rho}_{i_u}}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch05-refkernel-anchor}

the branch that sets `top_anchor`
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:30-38`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L30-L38)).
It uses the cell averages, so even on an isothermal column it is off by the factor
$\sinh a/a=1+a^2/6+O(a^4)$, $a=\Delta x_1/2H$ with $H=p/(\rho g)$ (`[C10]`). That offset is a column constant and drops
out of the rest balance (@eq-ch05-wbx1-rest holds for any $c$).

#### Cell pressure

On a uniform grid the cell pressure is the cell average of the quintic through the six faces
$i-\tfrac52,\dots,i+\tfrac52$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \tfrac{1}{1440}\big(&11\,p_{\mathrm{sf},i-5/2} - 93\,p_{\mathrm{sf},i-3/2} + 802\,p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2} \\
&\qquad + 802\,p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2} - 93\,p_{\mathrm{sf},i+3/2} + 11\,p_{\mathrm{sf},i+5/2}\big),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-refkernel-pref}

weights derived exactly in `[C1]` and coded as `w6`
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:140-156`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L140-L156)).
In the two cells next to an array end or a clamped wall the same average is taken over six one-sided faces, rows
`w6e` (`[C2]`, @sec-ch05-wallclamp). A value outside $[\min,\max]$ of the cell's own two face pressures is rejected
and the face mean is kept. Because the faces are exact up to $c$, $p_{\mathrm{ref},i}=\overline p_i+c+O(\Delta
x_1^6)$ (`[C13]`: fitted order 5.87 on an isothermal column, $n_1$ = 8, 16, 32).

On a non-uniform grid, where the relative spread of the face widths is $10^{-10}$ of their mean or more (`[C20]`),
the cell pressure is the log-mean

$$
p_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \frac{g\,\overline{\rho}_i\,\Delta x_{1,i}}{\ln(p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}/p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2})},
$$ {#eq-ch05-refkernel-logmean}

or the face mean when `ratio` is within $10^{-6}$ of one
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:181-186`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L181-L186)).
For an isothermal cell $p$ is exponential in $x_1$, and its cell average is exactly @eq-ch05-refkernel-logmean; for a
polytrope it is $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ (`[C9]`: relative error $1.5\times10^{-4}$ at $\Delta x_1=0.05$, order 2.02).

#### Density references

With $r_i=\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i$, the smoothed ratio is the binomial $r^{s}_i=\tfrac1{16}(r_{i-2}+4r_{i-1}+6r_i+4r_{i+1}+r_{i+2})$,
and the references are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i} &= p_{\mathrm{ref},i}\,r^{s}_i, \\
\rho_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2} &= p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}\,\tfrac12\big(r^{s}_{i-1}+r^{s}_i\big),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-refkernel-dens}

coded as `dref` and `dsf`
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:193-200`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L193-L200)),
with the binomial in `hydro_ref_x1_rop_smooth`
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:86-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L86-L108)).
At array index 0 the face density uses $r^s_0$ alone.

*Why smoothed.* Take the unsmoothed ratio instead, $\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i}=p_{\mathrm{ref},i}\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i$.
Then $\rho'_i=\overline\rho_i-p_{\mathrm{ref},i}\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i=\overline\rho_i\,p'_i/\overline p_i$, so
$\rho'/\overline\rho=p'/\overline p$ in every cell: the density perturbation carries no information the pressure
perturbation does not, and an entropy (buoyancy) anomaly is not reconstructed as a density perturbation at all. The
binomial keeps the reference on the large scales of the column only. It has unit sum, zero first moment and second
moment 1 in cells, and zero response at the grid scale (`[C3]`), so $r^{s}_i=r_i+\tfrac{\Delta x_1^2}{2}r''+O(\Delta
x_1^4)$. This re-derives the degeneracy stated in the comment above `hydro_ref_x1_rop_smooth`; the measurements behind
it are in `sources/canoe__tall_column_instability_TECH_REPORT.md` §§3d, 4-5.

*Face-density offset.* What the solver uses is $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}+\mathcal R[\overline\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]
=\mathcal R[\overline\rho]+\delta\rho_f$ with $\delta\rho_f=\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal R[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]$. Expanding
the ratio of averages, the binomial bias, the two-cell mean and the cell pressure,
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §2 obtains

$$
\delta\rho_f = \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{12}\big(p'R'+2pR''\big) + O(\Delta x_1^4),
$$ {#eq-ch05-refkernel-offset}

with $R=\rho/p$ the point ratio and primes $x_1$ derivatives (this paragraph only). `[C14]` measures $\delta\rho_f$ at
the middle face of a polytrope against fifth-order linear reconstruction and finds the ratio to
@eq-ch05-refkernel-offset 1.0022, 1.0005, 1.0001, 1.0000 at $n_1$ = 32 to 256, order 2.00.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the scan step, hence the rest balance. $O(\Delta x_1^6)$: the uniform cell pressure.
$O(\Delta x_1^2)$: the log-mean on non-isothermal cells, the smoothed ratio and the face density reference.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch05-refkernel-scan shows the stencils. The scan is serial along each column; the per-cell part reads six face
pressures and five ratios. The kernel runs once per $x_1$ sweep, in every RK stage, on cell averages (on plain means
under @sec-ch05-x1cent), including ghost cells: ghosts get face pressures from the upward scan and, without the wall
clamp, ghost ratios enter the binomial. Uniformity is decided once per block from its own `dx1f`.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
On a stretched $x_1$ grid the cell pressure is the log-mean, exact only for isothermal cells, so a column at rest is
at rest to round-off only after `balance_column`.
:::

1. **Non-uniform grids.** The log-mean is a different operator from the six-face rows, not a lower-order version of
   them, and the reconstruction weights are uniform-spacing on every grid. A stretched-grid rest residual of
   $7.37\times10^{-4}$, the same for every density form, is reported in chengcli/snapy#250
   (`sources/gh__ISSUE_THREADS_138-250.md`; measured before the pin, not re-run here); chengcli/snapy#280 tracks it.
   chengcli/snapy#280 also states that the face interpolation uses fixed rationals on stretched grids; at the pin the
   rationals are used only on a uniform block and the log-mean otherwise.
2. **No positivity guard on $\rho/p$.** The ratio divides by the cell pressure without a guard (chengcli/snapy#250
   §2). Not measured at the pin.
3. **One classification per block.** A grid uniform over part of the column gives different operators to different
   blocks; `balance_column` must make the same choice (@sec-ch05-balcol).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Keeps every reference stencil inside the owned cells at a physical $x_1$ wall: one-sided six-face
rows for the two wall cells, and $\rho/p$ continued past the wall from the two owned cells next to it.
**Switch.** YAML `dynamics/wb-wall-clamp`, default `true`.
**Order.** $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ second order at faces 0-2 next to each wall (first order with the wall cell repeated).
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-wallclamp-cont.
:::

The ghost cells of a reflecting wall hold the mirror image of the interior, which is the right input for the
Riemann solver but not a hydrostatic continuation of the column: a stratified profile mirrored at the wall has a kink.
Any reference stencil that reads a ghost therefore puts that kink into $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$
next to the wall. With the clamp on, the cell pressure of the two cells next to a physical wall uses one-sided
six-face rows, and the binomial of $\rho/p$ no longer reads ghosts. What it reads instead is the wall continuation:
the ratio continued linearly from the two owned cells where it rises towards the wall, and ln-linearly where it
falls. A plain repetition of the wall cell, the first version of the clamp, is exact only for constant $\rho/p$ and
leaves the face density reference first order at the three faces next to each wall.

The continuation changes only $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ at faces 0-2 and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ at cells 0-1 next to each
clamped wall (and their ghost rows); $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$, $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and the rest balance are untouched. It
applies with `SNAP_WB_REF4` off; with it on, @sec-ch05-wbref4 replaces the density reference with its own cubic wall
values. `balance_column` refuses to run with the clamp off.

*Aliases.* "wb-wall-clamp", "the wall closure", "linear/ln closure". The continuation arrived as three wall-closure
patches (linear, then ln-linear, then the two branches), kept as raw notes in `sources/team-notes/` and squash-merged
into the pin by chengcli/snapy#297.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-refkernel; cells are counted from the wall, $j=0$ the wall cell, and $r_j=\overline\rho_j/\overline p_j$.

#### The repeated wall cell is first order

Near the wall write $r_j=r_0+j\,a+O(\Delta x_1^2)$ with $a=r'\Delta x_1=O(\Delta x_1)$. Repeating $r_0$ for every
$j<0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
r^{s}_0 - r_0 &= \tfrac38\,a, \\
r^{s}_1 - r_1 &= \tfrac1{16}\,a,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wallclamp-repeat}

and errors $\tfrac{23}{32}a$, $\tfrac7{32}a$, $\tfrac1{32}a$ and $0$ in the face average $\tfrac12(r^s_{f-1}+r^s_f)$ at
faces 0 to 3 (`[C4]`, exact). Relative to $r$ these are fixed multiples of $(r'/r)\Delta x_1$, so the face density
reference is first order at faces 0-2. The even-parity perturbation ghosts (@sec-ch05-wbx1) copy the bias of
$\rho'=\overline\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ into the ghosts, so the solver's face densities there are first order too;
the mirror is not the source, the bias in $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is
(`docs/derivations/wb-ref-wall.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §3).

#### The continuation

Past a clamped wall the binomial reads, $k$ cells beyond the wall,

$$
r_{-k} =
\begin{cases}
r_0 + k\,(r_0 - r_1), & r_1 \le r_0,\\
r_0\,(r_0/r_1)^{k}, & r_1 > r_0,
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wallclamp-cont}

and $r_0$ if the value is not positive; the top wall is the mirror image. @eq-ch05-wallclamp-cont is
`hydro_ref_x1_wall_rop`
([`hydro_ref_x1_impl.h:68-72`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_ref_x1_impl.h#L68-L72)).
The binomial reproduces a linear profile exactly, so with the linear branch the $O(a)$ errors of
@eq-ch05-wallclamp-repeat vanish at faces 0-2; the ln-linear branch differs from it by $O(a^2)$, errors
$\tfrac{31}{32}a^2/r_0$, $\tfrac14a^2/r_0$, $\tfrac1{32}a^2/r_0$ (`[C5]`, exact series). Either way faces 0-2 keep
the interior's $O(\Delta x_1^2)$, and for constant $r$ the linear branch returns $r_0$ exactly, so an isothermal
column is unchanged bit for bit.

Each branch is unbounded on one side: the linear one reaches zero when $r$ rises steeply away from the wall
($r_{-3}=r_0(1-3d)$ with $d=(r_1-r_0)/r_0$), and the ln-linear one diverges when the neighbour is nearly empty. The
code takes the branch that stays closer to $r_0$, so for $r_1\ge0$ the continuation lies in
$[r_0(r_0/r_1)^k,\ r_0(1+k)]$ and is positive (`[C6]`, 60000 random samples, none outside).

#### The one-sided cell-pressure rows

The two wall cells take the cell average of the quintic through the six faces starting at the wall, weights `w6e`
derived exactly in `[C2]`: $(95/288, 1427/1440, -133/240, 241/720, -173/1440, 3/160)$ for the wall cell and
$(-3/160, 637/1440, 511/720, -43/240, 77/1440, -11/1440)$ for the next. They keep the sixth order of
@eq-ch05-refkernel-pref and read no ghost face.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the continuation for linear $r$ (linear branch), the rows for a quintic. Second
order: $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ at faces 0-2. The independent rebuild of `[C12]` gives the face-1 error first order with
the repeated wall cell (order 1.03) and second order with @eq-ch05-wallclamp-cont (order 2.01), $n_1$ = 32 to 256.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch05-wallclamp-continuation shows the two branches. The clamp applies on a side when the option is on and that
side is a physical boundary; the continuation additionally needs the wall side to own at least two cells, so that
only owned cells are read. The one-sided rows need the block to fit them (at least five interior cells, or a seam at
the other end), else the face mean is kept. The rule runs inside the kernel, in every call, on the CPU, CUDA and MPS
paths alike.

## Reference continuity across $x_1$ seams: anchor relay and ghost-row exchange ($x_1$ block split) {#sec-ch05-seam}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Makes the reference of a column split into several $x_1$ blocks equal to the reference of one
block: the face-pressure scan is relayed from block to block, top down, and the ghost rows of $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$
and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ are replaced by the neighbour's interior rows.
**Switch.** None. On whenever the layout splits $x_1$ ($p_z>1$) and $x_1$ is not periodic.
**Order.** Exact: a split column has the one-block reference up to the round-off of the chained scan.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-seam-relay.
:::

The reference kernel scans each column from an anchor at the top of the block (@sec-ch05-refkernel). On a column
split into $n_{b1}$ blocks along $x_1$, a block below the top one has no top of the domain to anchor at, and an
anchor from its own top cell would start a new scan with a different constant: the reference would jump at every
seam, and that jump would enter $p'=\overline p-p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ as a spurious perturbation every step. The relay
passes the running face pressure down instead, so the scan is one scan across the whole column. The second step
exchanges the reference's ghost rows, because the block-local quadrature of the ghost cells (one-sided rows, the
$[\min,\max]$ guard) does not reproduce the owner's interior values.

With both steps, the perturbation field the reconstruction sees is identical on both sides of every seam, so the
two sides compute the same seam-face states, whether the neighbour runs on another process or on another thread of
the same one.

*Aliases.* "the x1 relay" and "anchor relay" in comments; chengcli/snapy#254 (the seam jump), chengcli/snapy#259
(the in-process relay).

### Derivation

Number the blocks of one column $b=1..n_{b1}$ from the bottom, and write $i^{(b)}_s$, $i^{(b)}_u$ for the first and
last interior cell of block $b$. One block scans @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan downward from its top anchor. For blocks
$b<n_{b1}$ the anchor is not @eq-ch05-refkernel-anchor but the bottom-face pressure of the block above:

$$
p^{(b)}_{\mathrm{sf},\,i^{(b)}_u+1/2} = p^{(b+1)}_{\mathrm{sf},\,i^{(b+1)}_s-1/2},
$$ {#eq-ch05-seam-relay}

and block $n_{b1}$, which owns the domain top, uses @eq-ch05-refkernel-anchor. Since the two faces in
@eq-ch05-seam-relay are the same physical face, and @eq-ch05-refkernel-scan adds the same terms
$g\overline\rho_i\Delta x_{1,i}$ in the same order as a single block would, the face pressures of the split column
equal those of one block up to the round-off of the different summation boundaries. @eq-ch05-seam-relay is
`take_x1_anchor` in the block below
([`hydro.cpp:525-533`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L525-L533))
and `pass_x1_anchor` in the block above
([`hydro.cpp:577-579`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L577-L579)).

The cell pressure of a cell near the seam reads six faces, two beyond the cell on each side, so its value in the
block that owns it differs from the value the neighbour computes for the same cell in its ghost rows: the
neighbour has fewer faces there and uses one-sided rows or the face-mean fallback. Overwriting the $n_g$ ghost rows
of $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ with the owner's interior rows makes both blocks hold the owner's value
for every cell. Then $p'$ and $\rho'$ agree cell by cell across the seam, the reconstruction of each side reads the
same data in the stencil across the seam, and the seam-face states agree. The exchange is in `_hydro_ref_x1`, with
tags `kWbGhostUpTag` and `kWbGhostDnTag`
([`hydro.cpp:593-640`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L593-L640)).

*Exact and truncated.* Nothing is truncated: the split reference equals the one-block reference except for the
summation order of the relayed scan. Where the face density of @sec-ch05-wbref4 is used, its cell part runs before
this exchange and its face part after it, so the exchanged rows carry the fourth-order cell density and the faces are
computed from them on both sides. There is no executable check; the property is tested by the split-equals-one-block
tests below.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch05-seam-relay shows the two steps. The relay is serial along the column: each block waits for the block above
before it scans. Across processes the anchor is a point-to-point message (tag `0x7715`); between blocks of one
process it is posted to a board keyed by the receiving block and taken with a five-minute timeout, so local blocks
must run concurrently or from the top down. The ghost-row exchange uses the same pairing. Both run once per call of
`_hydro_ref_x1`, so in every RK stage, before the reconstruction.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Replaces the fraction $1-n_h$ of the $x_1$ gravity force $\rho g_1$ by the difference of the cell's
own reconstructed face pressures, and books the same replacement in the energy.
**Switch.** YAML `forcing/const-gravity/non-hydrostatic` $=n_h\in[0,1]$, default 1 (mode off).
**Requires.** $g_1\neq0$. Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` it uses the $r^2$ operator of @sec-ch05-x1cent.
**Order.** Exact cancellation at rest; away from rest the force is the difference between Riemann and reconstructed
face pressures.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-hsmode-force.
:::

In the default, non-hydrostatic mode ($n_h=1$) gravity enters as the body force $\overline\rho_ig_1$ of the constant
gravity forcing, and vertical motion responds to the imbalance between that force and the pressure fluxes. With
$n_h<1$ part of the body force is replaced by $(p^L_{i+1/2}-p^R_{i-1/2})/\Delta x_1$, the pressure difference between
the cell's own reconstructed states at its upper and lower face. At $n_h=0$ the vertical momentum of a cell then
changes only by the jumps $p^{*}-p^{L,R}$ that the Riemann solver introduces at its faces, which vanish in a column
at rest whatever the column is.

The value is checked to lie in $[0,1]$ when the YAML is read. The mode is independent of the well-balanced
reconstruction, but the two are normally used together: the face states it differences are the restored states of
@eq-ch05-wbx1-split.

*Aliases.* "hydrostatic-split pressure", "nh" in tests; `rho_grav` in the code.

### Derivation

Units as in @sec-ch05-wbx1. The constant gravity forcing adds $n_h\overline\rho_ig_1$ to the momentum and
$n_h\overline\rho_i\overline v_{1,i}g_1$ to the energy. The hydrostatic mode adds, in Cartesian geometry,

$$
\begin{aligned}
G_i &= \frac{p^{L}_{i+1/2} - p^{R}_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x_{1,i}}, \\
\Delta(\rho v_1)_i &= \Delta t\,(1-n_h)\,G_i, \\
\Delta E_i &= \Delta t\,(1-n_h)\,\overline v_{1,i}\,G_i,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-hsmode-force}

with $p^{L}_{i+1/2}$ the left state at the upper face and $p^{R}_{i-1/2}$ the right state at the lower face, both
belonging to cell $i$. $G$ is `rho_grav`
([`hydro_forward.cpp:389-397`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L389-L397)),
applied by the increments that use `non_hydrostatic`
([`hydro_forward.cpp:901-906`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L901-L906)).
At $n_h=0$ the momentum balance of cell $i$ becomes

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\overline{\rho v_1})_i = -\frac{\Delta_i[\rho v_1^2]}{\Delta x_1}
- \frac{(p^{*}-p^{L})_{i+1/2} - (p^{*}-p^{R})_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x_1} ,
$$

so the cell's own pressure difference no longer drives it; only the face jumps do. At rest the two states of every
face agree and $p^{*}=p^{L}=p^{R}$, so the force vanishes exactly for any column, balanced or not (`[C19]`). For
$0<n_h<1$ the force is the blend of the two forms.

Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` on spherical-polar grids the pressure force is
$-(A_{i+1/2}p^{*}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{*}_{i-1/2})/V_i+S_i$ with the source $S_i$ of @eq-ch05-x1cent-source, and $G$ takes
the same operator on the cell's own states,
$G_i=(A_{i+1/2}p^{L}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{R}_{i-1/2})/V_i-S_i$, so the two cancel at rest again
(`docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §4). This form is the branch
that calls `x1_pressure_source`
([`hydro_forward.cpp:515-539`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L515-L539)).

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the cancellation at rest, in both forms. Away from rest the momentum source has the
accuracy of $p^{*}-p^{L,R}$, which depends on the reconstruction and the Riemann solver (Chapter 4).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch05-hsmode-cell shows the quantities. $G$ is formed right after the $x_1$ reconstruction (and the
immersed-solid face treatment), from the interior faces of each cell, and applied once per stage together with the
other source increments of `HydroImpl::forward`. It is explicit. The energy row books $\overline v_1G$, and the
gravity-work bookkeeping of Chapter 6 counts the same term (`original_gravity_work`).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Moves a column of cell averages, at fixed $p/\rho$ per cell, to the fixed point
$\overline p=p_{\mathrm{ref}}(\overline p)+C$ of @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest, so that the solver starts it at rest.
**Switch.** None: an API function, `balance_column` in C++ and in the Python package, called by initial-condition
builders. Requires `wb-wall-clamp` on, at least five cells, positive $p$ and $\rho$.
**Order.** Fixed point to a residual below `rtol` (default $10^{-10}$, at most 120 sweeps).
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-balcol-iter.
:::

A column integrated from the continuum hydrostatic equation is balanced to the truncation error of that integration,
not to the scheme's own discrete balance. The well-balanced reconstruction then sees a perturbation $p'$ that is not
constant and turns its variation into a standing force on an atmosphere that should be at rest. `balance_column`
removes that force before the run starts: it iterates the column onto the discrete rest state, holding the
temperature of each cell fixed for ideal mixtures, and returns the balanced column, the residual and the number of
updates. The fixed point is defined only up to a free constant $C$, so the column moves; any pinned quantity (surface
pressure, column mass) has to be re-pinned by the caller.

Under `SNAP_WB_REF4` on a non-uniform grid it iterates against the switched cell pressure, which is the fixed point
the solver then enforces. Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` it balances only a column declared Cartesian.

*Aliases.* "the balance-ic projection" (the bryan example's `balance-ic`), chengcli/snapy#250 D1.

### Derivation

Units as in @sec-ch05-wbx1. Let the column hold $n_1\ge5$ cells with no ghosts and both ends physical, and let
$\theta_i=\overline p_i/\overline\rho_i$ be taken once from the input. One sweep evaluates the reference kernel on the
whole column, reads the gauge at the top cell and updates

$$
\begin{aligned}
C &= \overline{p}_{n_1-1} - p_{\mathrm{ref},n_1-1}, \\
\overline{p}_i &\leftarrow p_{\mathrm{ref},i}(\overline{p},\overline{\rho}) + C, \\
\overline{\rho}_i &\leftarrow \overline{p}_i/\theta_i ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-balcol-iter}

and stops when

$$
\varepsilon = \max_i\frac{\lvert \overline{p}_i - p_{\mathrm{ref},i} - C\rvert}{\overline{\rho}_i\,g\,\Delta x_{1,i}} < \mathrm{rtol} .
$$ {#eq-ch05-balcol-res}

@eq-ch05-balcol-iter and @eq-ch05-balcol-res are the loop that calls `call_hydro_ref_x1`
([`balance_column.cpp:85-104`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/balance_column.cpp#L85-L104)).
A fixed point of @eq-ch05-balcol-iter satisfies @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest with $c=C$, so it is at rest in the solver. The
residual is checked before the update, so the returned column is the one it describes and an already balanced
column comes back after zero updates. $\varepsilon$ bounds the residual acceleration in units of $g$: a perturbation
difference $\delta p'$ across a cell drives an acceleration $\delta p'/(\overline\rho\Delta x_1)$.

The gauge is read at the top cell, where the pressure is lowest, so the column moves least where it is thinnest; the
code comment records that a gauge at the bottom diverges on a deep column. Holding $\theta_i$ fixed holds the
temperature fixed for `ideal-gas` and for `ideal-moist` at fixed mass fractions. No convergence proof exists; the
sweep is a contraction in practice, and the check shows it on a column that is not balanced to begin with
(`[C15]`: a $\beta=0.3$ polytrope with a $10^{-3}$ pressure bump at fixed $p/\rho$, $n_1=64$, residual
$4.64\times10^{-2}$ to $1.03\times10^{-11}$ in 12 updates, $p/\rho$ unchanged to $1.5\times10^{-16}$).

*Why the result transfers to the blocks.* With the wall clamp on, the reference of a block's interior reads only owned
cells at a physical wall (@sec-ch05-wallclamp), so a ghost-free column and a block holding the same cells get the same
$p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, bitwise; that is what the first test below asserts. Without the clamp the wall rows read ghost
faces that the ghost-free column does not have, and the two disagree, which is why the function refuses to run.
$\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ differs at the bottom cell only (its fallback keys on the array index), and it plays no part in
the fixed point.

*Exact and truncated.* The returned column satisfies @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest to $\varepsilon<\mathrm{rtol}$; nothing is
truncated beyond that.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Replaces the kernel's density reference by $p_{\mathrm{ref}}F(\rho/p)$ with a fourth-order filter
$F$, and the face density by the face value of that same cell field, so the face-density offset is $O(\Delta x_1^4)$;
on non-uniform grids it also replaces the cell pressure by a cubic average.
**Switch.** Environment variable `SNAP_WB_REF4`, read once per process, default off; implied by
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`. Requires $n_g\ge3$ (checked at setup).
**Order.** $\delta\rho_f=O(\Delta x_1^4)$; $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ is never changed, so the rest balance is the kernel's.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref.
:::

The kernel's density reference is second order: the binomial smoothing biases $\rho/p$ by $\tfrac{\Delta x_1^2}{2}r''$,
and its face density is not the face value of its own cell density, so the solver's face density carries the offset
@eq-ch05-refkernel-offset. That offset enters the $x_1$ mass flux at linear order and, through it, the gravity work. The
switch removes it with two operators: a five-point filter with zero second and third moments, which keeps the
reference fourth order while still removing the two-cell mode, and a face value taken from the quartic through the
primitive of the cell reference, so that face and cell are consistent by construction. On a non-uniform grid it also
replaces the log-mean cell pressure by the average of a cubic through four face pressures.

Guards keep the kernel's values wherever the new ones would leave the local range or the column is under-resolved,
and the cell part runs before the seam exchange of @sec-ch05-seam, the face part after it. With the corrected-PE face
work of Chapter 6 on (its default with `gravity-work: face`) the one-step spurious stratification of a neutral column
converges at about fourth order with the switch and second order without it.

*Aliases.* "Leg W" in `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md`; `SNAPY_WB_REF_EXACT` in the specification
`sources/gw__NEXTPR_spec_wbref_exact.md`; #289 in comments.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-refkernel; indices are cell indices and $r_i=\overline\rho_i/\overline p_i$. The derivation is
`docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §§2-7, re-written here and checked by
`[C3]`, `[C7]`, `[C8]`, `[C14]`.

#### Cell density

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{ref},i} &= p_{\mathrm{ref},i}\,(Fr)_i, \\
F &= \tfrac1{16}(-1,\,4,\,10,\,4,\,-1).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-dref}

$F$ has unit sum, zero first, second and third moments and fourth moment $-\tfrac32$ in cell units, and zero response
at $k\Delta x_1=\pi$ (`[C3]`), so $Fq=q+O(\Delta x_1^4)$ and the two-cell mode is still removed; its reach, $\pm2$, is
the binomial's, so ghost depth and seam exchange are unchanged. With $p_{\mathrm{ref}}=\overline p+c+O(\Delta x_1^6)$
(@sec-ch05-refkernel) the cell reference is $\overline\rho+cR+O(\Delta x_1^4)$, and the smooth $cR$ is carried
consistently by the face value below. @eq-ch05-wbref4-dref is built in `wb_ref4_stencils` as the filter row `F`
([`wb_ref4.cpp:120-158`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp#L120-L158))
and applied in `wb_ref4_cells` as `fr`
([`wb_ref4.cpp:263-272`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp#L263-L272)).

At a clamped wall the two values past the wall are cubic extrapolations of the four owned cells nearest it,
$r_0..r_3$ counted from the wall:

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_{-1} &= 4r_0 - 6r_1 + 4r_2 - r_3, \\
r_{-2} &= 10r_0 - 20r_1 + 15r_2 - 4r_3 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-cubic}

All five stencil values of the first two cells then lie on one cubic, which $F$ reproduces, so $(Fr)_0=r_0$ and
$(Fr)_1=r_1$ for any data (`[C7]`): filtering with these wall values and leaving the two end cells unfiltered are the
same reference. Ghosts are never read.

#### Face density

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{sf},f} &= P'(x_{1,f}), \\
P(x_{1,s+j}) &= \sum_{k<j}\rho_{\mathrm{ref},s+k}\,\Delta x_{1,s+k},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-face}

with $P$ the quartic through the primitive at the five faces $j=0..4$ (four cells), window $s=f-2$ kept inside the owned cells at a
clamped wall, physical spacing. On a uniform grid the weights on $\rho_{\mathrm{ref},s..s+3}$ are $(-1,7,7,-1)/12$ in the
interior, $(25,-23,13,-3)/12$ at the wall face and $(3,13,-5,1)/12$ at the next (`[C8]`). The face is exact for cubic
point profiles on any grid, so $\delta\rho_f=\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}-\mathcal R[\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}]=O(\Delta x_1^4)$ (`[C14]`:
mid-column offset $3.2\times10^{-12}$ to $2.8\times10^{-16}$ relative from $n_1$ = 32 to 256, fitted order 4.68, against
order 2.00 for the kernel). @eq-ch05-wbref4-face is built as the weights `awt`
([`wb_ref4.cpp:195-221`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp#L195-L221))
and applied by `wb_ref4_faces`
([`wb_ref4.cpp:276-286`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp#L276-L286)).

#### Non-uniform cell pressure

On a non-uniform grid the cell pressure becomes the cell average of the cubic $\tilde p$ through the face pressures at
faces $i-1..i+2$ (window inside the owned faces at a clamped wall), by three-point Gauss-Legendre, exact for a cubic:

$$
p_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \frac{1}{\Delta x_{1,i}}\int_{x_{1,i-1/2}}^{x_{1,i+1/2}}\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}x_1
= \sum_{q=1}^{3}\frac{w_q}{2}\,\tilde p\big(x_{1,i}+\xi_q\tfrac{\Delta x_{1,i}}{2}\big),
$$ {#eq-ch05-wbref4-pnu}

with nodes $\xi_q=0,\pm\sqrt{3/5}$ and weights $w_q=8/9,5/9$, the non-uniform branch of `wb_ref4_stencils` with the Gauss weights `gw`
([`wb_ref4.cpp:165-193`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp#L165-L193)).
A value outside the cell's two face pressures keeps the log-mean. This moves the discrete fixed point of a non-uniform
column by $O(\Delta x_1^2)$, so `balance_column` iterates against it (@sec-ch05-balcol). On a uniform grid the
six-face $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is kept.

#### Guards and rest balance

A cell whose $(Fr)_i$ lies outside $[\min,\max]$ of $r$ over cells $i-1..i+1$, with relative margin $10^{-10}$, keeps the
kernel's ratio; a face outside its two neighbouring cell references keeps the kernel's face. A cell with
$\lvert\ln(p_{\mathrm{sf},i-1/2}/p_{\mathrm{sf},i+1/2})\rvert>0.5$, fewer than two cells per pressure scale height, is
flagged, the flag is dilated by two cells, and flagged cells and faces next to them keep the kernel's values; ghosts
past a clamped wall do not count. The flag reads $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ at most three cells away, which is why $n_g\ge3$ is
required: then both sides of an $x_1$ seam compute the same flag. The threshold, dilation and margin are design
choices, not derived. Since $p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ is never changed and on a uniform grid neither is $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, the
rest state @eq-ch05-wbx1-rest is the kernel's.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the end-cell identity, the face weights for cubics, @eq-ch05-wbref4-pnu for cubics.
$O(\Delta x_1^4)$: $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\delta\rho_f$ in the interior. At the three faces next to a wall the note
gives $O(\Delta x_1^3)$ (the anchor constant through the even ghosts); not re-checked here.

@fig-ch05-wbref4-stencils shows the stencils. The stencils and weights are built once per block, on the CPU in double

after it, so a column split along $x_1$ gets the same faces as one block. A block with a clamped wall and fewer than

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** On spherical-polar blocks, feeds every $x_1$ map (reconstruction, scan, reference) the plain means
of the cells instead of their $r^2$ means, and replaces the radial pressure source by the $r$-moment of a quintic, so a
hydrostatic column of $r^2$ means is balanced to round-off.
**Switch.** Environment variable `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, read once per process, default off. Implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`.
Requires $n_g\ge3$. Acts on `spherical-polar` only.
**Order.** Conversion exact to degree 4; rest exact for densities of degree $\le4$.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-x1cent-source.
:::

A finite-volume cell on a spherical-polar grid holds the $r^2$ mean of a quantity, whose centroid sits
$h^2/(6\overline r)$ above the mid-radius. Every $x_1$ cell-to-face map of the solver, from the WENO weights to the
scan and the six-face cell pressure, is a formula for plain means. Fed $r^2$ means they are off by $O(h^2/r)$: the face
values, the scan step, and the pressure force, whose plain difference balances gravity only against the wrong scan.
The switch converts the inputs of the maps, for the maps only, to plain means with a five-cell stencil exact to degree
4, and makes the radial pressure force the $r^2$ mean of the gradient of a quintic through six face pressures. The
reference on plain means is then the Cartesian one, and the switch implies `SNAP_WB_REF4` so that it is fourth order.

On Cartesian blocks the switch only implies `SNAP_WB_REF4`; on cubed-sphere blocks it does nothing (their $x_{1v}$ is
the mid-radius). `balance_column` balances only a column declared Cartesian under it.

*Aliases.* #289 legs (i)-(iii) in comments; "the centroid switch".

### Derivation

Units: $r$ and $h$ [m]; $A_{i\pm1/2}=r_{i\pm1/2}^2$ and $V_i=(r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3)/3$ are per unit solid angle, as the
code forms them. $\langle q\rangle_i=V_i^{-1}\int r^2q\,\mathrm{d}r$ is the $r^2$ mean, $\overline q_i=h_i^{-1}\int q\,\mathrm{d}r$ the plain
mean, and $x=(r-\overline r_i)/h_i$ the local coordinate. Re-written from
`docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §§1-5.

#### The defect

Expanding $q$ about the mid-radius,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle q\rangle_i &= \overline q_i + \delta_i\,q'(\overline r_i) + O(h^4/\overline r^2), \\
\delta_i &= \frac{2h_i^2\,\overline r_i}{h_i^2 + 12\,\overline r_i^2} = \frac{h_i^2}{6\overline r_i} - \frac{h_i^4}{72\,\overline r_i^3} + \cdots
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-defect}

(`[C18]`, exact). Each uniform-measure map fed $\langle q\rangle$ is off by $\delta q'=O(h^2/r)$; in particular the scan
step becomes $gh\langle\rho\rangle$ instead of $g\int\rho\,\mathrm{d}r=gh\overline\rho$, and the perturbation of a resting
column is $O(h^2/r)$ instead of a constant.

#### Plain means

For the $x_1$ maps only, each primitive row is replaced by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overline q_i &= \sum_{k=0}^{4} c_{i,k}\,\langle q\rangle_{s_i+k}, \\
\sum_k c_{i,k}\,\langle x^n\rangle_{s_i+k} &= \overline{x^n}_i = \big(1,\ 0,\ \tfrac1{12},\ 0,\ \tfrac1{80}\big)_n,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-conv}

for the monomials $n=0..4$, window $s_i=\max(\mathrm{lo},\min(\mathrm{hi}-4,i-2))$, centred, inside the owned cells at a physical wall and inside the
array at a seam. The moments are integrated by four-point Gauss-Legendre, exact for degree 6, and the $5\times5$ system
is solved once per block. The conversion is exact for degree 4 and not 5, on uniform and stretched grids and in the
wall windows, and its weights sum to 1 (`[C16]`). @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv is `x1_plain_mean_stencils`
([`x1_centroid.cpp:104-155`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp#L104-L155)).
Ghosts past a clamped wall get the mirrored correction of the owned cells, odd for the normal velocity, in
`x1_plain_means`
([`x1_centroid.cpp:157-182`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp#L157-L182));
at a seam the outer ghosts' windows are off-centre, so their plain means are replaced by the neighbour's.

#### The pressure source

With $\tilde p$ the quintic through the six face pressures nearest cell $i$ (window over faces, one-sided at a wall,
reaching two faces past a seam), the radial pressure source is

$$
S_i = \frac{2}{V_i}\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}} r\,\tilde p\,\mathrm{d}r = \sum_{j=0}^{5}w_{i,j}\,p^{*}_{s+j},
$$ {#eq-ch05-x1cent-source}

and integration by parts, with $\tilde p$ through both faces of the cell, gives
$-(A_{i+1/2}p^{*}_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}p^{*}_{i-1/2})/V_i+S_i=-V_i^{-1}\int r^2\tilde p'\,\mathrm{d}r$: the net pressure force is
the $r^2$ mean of $-\partial_r\tilde p$. A constant pressure gives $S_iV_i=A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2}$ exactly, with $V_i$ in the
cube form of the cell volume (`[C17]`, both identities in exact rationals). @eq-ch05-x1cent-source is
`x1_pressure_source_stencils`
([`x1_centroid.cpp:184-222`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp#L184-L222)),
used in place of the plain difference by the branch that tests `exact_x1`
([`spherical_polar.cpp:251-264`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L251-L264)).
The hydrostatic mode takes the same operator (@sec-ch05-hsmode).

#### Rest balance

On a hydrostatic column of $r^2$ means: the conversion gives $\overline\rho$ to $O(h^6/r)$; the scan then gives the
exact face pressures plus one constant; the reference on plain means is the Cartesian fourth-order one; and the net
force $-V^{-1}\int r^2(\tilde p'+g\rho)\,\mathrm{d}r$ has the constant drop out. For a density of degree $\le4$ every step
is exact and the column is balanced exactly, which is the oracle of the test.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: the conversion for degree 4, both source identities, rest for degree $\le4$. For a
smooth column the curvature part of the residual is $O(h^6/r)$; what remains is the truncation of the reference itself.
Ratios of means (the Favre velocity, $T=p/\rho$, $\rho/p$ inside $F$) are not made exact (@sec-ch05-oneoverr).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch05-x1cent-window shows the windows. In `HydroImpl::forward` the plain-mean view `wx1` is computed before the
reference, its seam ghost rows are taken from the neighbour, and the reconstruction and the reference read it; the
primitives themselves are unchanged. After the Riemann solve the two ghost face pressures each side of a seam are taken
from the neighbour, so the source window is the centred one-block window. Everything runs in every RK stage,
explicitly; the stencils are built once per block in double precision.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it is.** The part of the $1/R$ error of a spherical column that survives `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` and
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`: an $O(h^2/R)$ term from reconstructing the Favre velocity
$\langle\rho w\rangle/\langle\rho\rangle$ as if it were a plain mean.
**Switch.** None; a property of the scheme. The related switches are `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` (Chapter 4),
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (@sec-ch05-x1cent) and `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` (Chapter 6).
**Order.** $O(h^2/R)$.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-oneoverr-favre.
:::

On a spherical-polar grid the $r^2$ cell measure adds terms of relative size $h/R$ to every cell-to-face map, and the
divergence adds a $2/r$ factor to every flux error. Chapter 4's covariance corrections and the plain-mean maps of
@sec-ch05-x1cent remove the leading such terms of the face fluxes, the reference and the pressure force. What remains
is not a defect of any map but of an input: the $x_1$ velocity the maps reconstruct is a ratio of two $r^2$ means, not a
mean, and the conversion of @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv makes means plain, not ratios exact. This section records that
remainder, its signature, and what evidence exists for it at the pin; it has no code of its own.

*Aliases.* "the 1/R term", "leg (d)" of #289; "hypothesis H1" in `sources/gw__ONEOVERR_split_RESULT.md`.

### Derivation

Notation as in @sec-ch05-x1cent; $R$ [m] is the radius of the column, $w=v_1$. The stored velocity of cell $i$ is the
Favre mean $\tilde w_i=\langle\rho w\rangle_i/\langle\rho\rangle_i$. Expanding $\rho$ and $w$ about the mid-radius with the
moments of @eq-ch05-x1cent-defect, and the plain mean likewise,

$$
\tilde w_i - \overline w_i = \frac{h_i^2}{12}\,\frac{\rho'\,w'}{\rho} + \delta_i\,w' + O(h^4) ,
$$ {#eq-ch05-oneoverr-favre}

where the first term is the Cartesian covariance of a density-weighted mean and the second the centroid offset of the
$r^2$ measure (this paragraph only: primes are $r$-derivatives; derived for linear $\rho$ and $w$ in `[C21]`, exact in
sympy). The conversion of @eq-ch05-x1cent-conv treats $\tilde w$ as an $r^2$ mean and so removes the $\delta_iw'$ part;
the covariance part stays. Reconstructing the converted value with weights for plain means therefore leaves an $O(h^2)$
face error, which the $2/r$ of the radial divergence turns into an $O(h^2/R)$ tendency. The
same holds for $T=p/\rho$ and for $\rho/p$ inside the reference filter. The expansion follows
`docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §6; the harness and the
$+g/(6c_pR)$ signature of the remainder in the effective stratification are in `sources/study__next-1overR_README.md`
§§0-3, and the completeness of the face fluxes to $O(h^4)$ including $h^2/R$ is
`sources/gw__ONEOVERR_split_RESULT.md` §§1-2.

*Exact and truncated.* The remainder is $O(h^2/R)$ and vanishes for $R\to\infty$ (Cartesian).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Two older wall treatments of the non-well-balanced $x_1$ path: an isentropic extrapolation of $p$ and
$\rho$ into the wall ghosts (defined, never called) and a copy of the right state's $p$ and $\rho$ into the left state
at the wall face (called only on the non-well-balanced path with gravity on).
**Switch.** None.
**Status.** Effectively unreachable: with gravity on and any EOS other than `shallow-water` the well-balanced path of
@sec-ch05-wbx1 runs instead, and the shallow-water EOS has no pressure row for these routines to use.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch05-legacy-copy.
:::

Before the well-balanced reconstruction, a stratified column at a wall was handled by filling the ghost cells with an
isentropic continuation of the wall cell and by making the two states at the wall face agree. Both routines are still
in the code. The ghost fill's call in `HydroImpl::forward` is commented out; the face copy runs only on the $x_1$ path
taken when `wb_x1` is false and gravity is on, a combination no configuration reaches with a pressure row.

### Derivation

The face copy sets, at the lower wall face $i_s-\tfrac12$ (and symmetrically at the upper one),

$$
\begin{aligned}
p^{L}_{i_s-1/2} &\leftarrow p^{R}_{i_s-1/2}, \\
\rho^{L}_{i_s-1/2} &\leftarrow \rho^{R}_{i_s-1/2},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-legacy-copy}

in `_revise_x1inner_lr`
([`hydro.cpp:448-453`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L448-L453)),
so the Riemann solver sees no pressure jump at the wall. The ghost fill holds $K=p/\rho^\gamma$ of the wall cell and
integrates $\mathrm{d}(p^{a})/\mathrm{d}x_1=-a\,g/K^{1/\gamma}$, $a=(\gamma-1)/\gamma$, cell by cell into the ghosts, the
isentropic hydrostatic profile, in `_revise_x1inner_ghost`
([`hydro.cpp:462-480`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro.cpp#L462-L480)).
Neither is used at the pin, so neither has a check.
